hero.title: Lan Wei
hero.description: I am a PhD student in Robotics at Imperial College London, advised by Dr Dandan Zhang. My research focuses on Embodied AI, with particular interests in physics-grounded multimodal world models, visuo-tactile perception, sim-to-real learning, efficient vision-language-action models, and fast diffusion inference. I am particularly interested in building physically grounded and computationally efficient AI systems that can perceive, reason about, and interact with the real world. Before joining Imperial, I received my M.Eng. in Computer Science and Technology from the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and my B.Eng. from Xiamen University.

data.summary: Co-organized two workshops on safe and physical world models for embodied AI at ECCV 2026 and IROS 2026. Thanks to all organizers, speakers, and participants!
Our work on safe and trustworthy robotic manipulation with constrained multimodal LLMs was selected for an oral presentation at the IROS 2026 PWMS Workshop.
Our TacVerse paper on cross-sensor vision-based tactile perception was accepted to Advanced Robotics Research. Thanks to all collaborators!
Three papers were accepted to IROS 2026. Thanks to all collaborators!
Our paper on fast diffusion model decoding was accepted to ICML 2026 (acceptance rate: 26.6%).
Two papers were accepted to MARSS 2026.
Honored to receive the 2026 Early Career Development Grant from the Imperial I-X Women in AI Network (IX-WAI).
Congratulations to the Master's students I co-supervise with Dr Dandan Zhang on having four papers accepted to ICRA 2026!
Happy to receive the IROS 2025 IEEE RAS Travel Support Award, with a travel grant of $1,500.
Our paper on physics-informed optical microrobot depth estimation was accepted to IEEE CBS 2025 and selected as a Best Bionic System Award Finalist.
Our paper on optical microrobot pose and depth perception won the Best Student Paper Award with the highest score at MARSS 2025!
Our paper on multi-pipette localization for robot-assisted patch-clamp was accepted to IROS 2025.
Our paper introducing a dataset and benchmarks for optical microrobot pose and depth perception was accepted to MARSS 2025.
I joined Imperial College London as a fully funded PhD student in Robotics.
I graduated from the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) with an M.Eng. in Computer Science and Technology.
